author: goldenwalrus909
body:
Hello, fellow Avicus forum user!
Today I will be talking about my opinions on why ban appeals should be on the forums, as you can tell from the title.
So, first of all, I don't understand why they should be in email form. If you get banned from a server, the first thing you'd think of doing would be to go to the forums and tell people that you should be unbanned, not make an email that takes forever to get answered and makes you wonder if anyone actually read it. That might make you want to post on the forums, so you understand that you did the right thing, not just send an email to some random person. This makes a lot of spam posts that are always locked by some mod saying to email. 
It would be so much better if it was just on the forums! In the Administration section, below Staff Applications, there would be a ban appeal sub-forum that you could post your appeal on without anyone else seeing it besides you and the mods. This would really help players that don't know what they're doing because it would be obvious and more less questionable. This would highly reduce the amount of posts about ban appeals because the banned player would look for a place on the forums to make a post and wouldn't have to question people about where to post it. 
Maybe there would also be a number next to the sub-forum telling the mods how many new posts there are in it, so they can check them out and see if they should be appealed or not.
So, the question is: why not? It would be easy, self-explanatory, and stop a bunch of spam. What do you think of this matter?
If you have any approval, criticism, or ideas, comment below! :3 
Have a good day! c:

-Love, Goldie

replies.author: Joao_Victor
replies.body:
This has been suggested lots of times, and has one huge flaw.

You register in-game with /register, if you're banned, and didn't make a forums account before you were banned, then you're out of luck.

Also, ever since Senior Mods were given access to the support e-mails, we've been very efficient with answering e-mails.

If there was a way to register without going on in-game, then +1.
